title: Proper morphisms and etale-origin torsion sheaves satisfy the ph comparison hypotheses
statement:
Let $S$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes and compatible small site presentations as in [def-weil-size-convention]. On the category $\mathcal C=\mathrm{Sch}/S$ use the big etale topology and the big ph topology [def-trf-ph-scheme-site]. For $X\in\mathcal C$, write $B_X=(\mathrm{Sch}/X)_{\mathrm{Et}}$, $P_X=(\mathrm{Sch}/X)_{ph}$, and let $\pi_X:\mathrm{Sh}(B_X)\to\mathrm{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{Et}})$ be the big-to-small etale morphism of [lem-trf-big-small-etale-exact-retraction]. The etale topology is coarser than the ph topology. Write $\epsilon_X:\mathrm{Sh}(P_X)\to\mathrm{Sh}(B_X)$ for the comparison geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism] induced by the identity, with direct image the identity on underlying presheaves and inverse image ph sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ induces the relocalization morphism $f_{\mathrm{Et}}:\mathrm{Sh}(B_X)\to\mathrm{Sh}(B_Y)$, whose inverse image sends $H$ to the sheaf $(U\to X)\mapsto H(U\to X\to Y)$. Write $R^if_{\mathrm{Et},*}$ for its ordinary right derived direct images on abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $\mathcal P$ be the class of proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism] in $\mathcal C$, and let $\mathcal A'_X\subset\mathrm{Ab}(B_X)$ be the full subcategory of sheaves isomorphic to $\pi_X^{-1}F$ for torsion abelian sheaves $F$ on $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Then each $\mathcal A'_X$ is a weak Serre subcategory: it contains zero and is closed under isomorphisms, kernels and cokernels of morphisms between its objects, and extensions. Moreover the following five properties hold.

(1) For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathcal P$ and any $Y'\to Y$, the fibre product $X\times_Y Y'$ exists and $X\times_Y Y'\to Y'$ belongs to $\mathcal P$.

(2) For every $f:X\to Y$, the restriction functor $f_{\mathrm{Et}}^{-1}$ sends $\mathcal A'_Y$ into $\mathcal A'_X$.

(3) For every $H'\in\mathcal A'_X$, its underlying presheaf on $\mathrm{Sch}/X$ satisfies the ph sheaf condition.

(4) For every $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathcal P$, every $H'\in\mathcal A'_X$, and every $i\geq0$, one has $R^if_{\mathrm{Et},*}H'\in\mathcal A'_Y$.

(5) Every ph covering $\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ admits a refinement $\{W_{jk}\to U\}_{j\in J,k\in K_j}$ factoring through an etale covering $\{V_j\to U\}_{j\in J}$, singleton ph coverings $\{W_j\to V_j\}$ whose morphisms lie in $\mathcal P$, and etale coverings $\{W_{jk}\to W_j\}_{k\in K_j}$. Here refinement means that each composite $W_{jk}\to U$ factors through one of the $U_i\to U$. All the covering families are small in the chosen universe; torsion requires no common annihilator and no invertibility of torsion orders.
